messages:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: [INCIDENT] OTEL export errors to New Relic (us-west-2). Exporter showing sustained 429s/504s, exporter queue length growing across otel-collector replicas. Assigned severity: P2. Runbook: /runbooks/otel-export-failure. Thread opened at 2026-03-15T09:12:57Z

alice_cheng: ack — I'm taking first stab. grabbing latest logs and checking which customers affected.

ben_kim: seeing the same on dashboards — trace-export error rate jumped at ~09:12 UTC. Dropped spans for a subset of high-volume customers. No backend 5xxs reported by services.

carol_ops: logs from otel-collector (replica-2):
```
2026-03-15T09:12:18Z exporter/http: send failed, status=429, body="rate limited"
2026-03-15T09:12:18Z exporter/http: retrying in 120ms
2026-03-15T09:12:19Z exporter/queue: enqueue failed, queue_size=12000, max_queue=12000
2026-03-15T09:12:20Z exporter/http: send failed, status=504
```
queue growth correlates with CPU/memory spike on collector pods.

devops-oncall: is there any indication this is an NR-side throttle (global) or only our account/ingest keys? Can someone open a vendor ticket?

alice_cheng: opening support ticket with New Relic now. NR account IDs and sample trace IDs attached. ticket created: NR-237912. I included ingestion timestamps and sample span ids.

kate_support: customer-impact note: APM dashboards will show missing traces and slow trace load for customers in us-west-2 between 09:12-09:40 UTC. Logs, metrics still intact. I'll draft a short status message for affected customers (APM traces degraded, dashboards missing spans).

ml-runtime-oncall: quick mitigation options: 1) reduce sampling probability to reduce export volume 2) switch exporter to buffered/disk mode 3) temporarily route traces to internal S3 bucket for later bulk upload 4) disable export to NR for the highest-volume services. Which is fastest?

carol_ops: fastest is reduce sampling and disable high-volume exporters. We can patch otel-collector ConfigMap to change tail sampling or parent-based sampler. Example patch (admin API):
```
# set sampler to 5% via environment toggle (collector supports this env var)
kubectl -n observability set env deployment/otel-collector OTEL_SAMPLING_PROBABILITY=0.05
```
or edit the ConfigMap snippet: 
```
service:
  pipelines:
    traces:
      receivers: [otlp]
      processors: [batch, memory_limiter, probabilistic_sampler]
      exporters: [newrelic]

processors:
  probabilistic_sampler:
    sampling_percentage: 5
```
apply with `kubectl apply -f otel-config.yaml`

ben_kim: I can push the sampler change and scale down the exporters for the top 3 noisy services. Doing a canary patch to one collector first.

devops-oncall: do that but preserve one collector with original config for debugging. Also enable verbose logs on one replica and capture the 429 response headers (NR often supplies x-rate-limit info).

alice_cheng: deployed sampler change to canary collector (replica-0). Observed exporter rate drop ~70% within 90s, queue length decreased. Replicas still reporting occasional 429s but no queue overflow.

carol_ops: NR support replied: "We see increased defenses triggered on your ingestion key for account <redacted>. We're investigating. We recommend exponential backoff + reduced concurrency. If you can provide list of account IDs, we can temporarily raise the threshold." They've asked for account IDs and representative trace IDs (I already provided).

kate_support: proposed customer-facing blurb (short):
"We're seeing degraded trace ingestion to New Relic in us-west-2 causing missing traces for some customers. We're applying mitigations to reduce volume and will update within 2 hours. Metrics and logs are unaffected."

simon_product: tagging customer success for any premium accounts that might be impacted. Also, do we have any feature rollouts that started at 09:10 that could explain spike?

ben_kim: quick check — no known rollout. High-volume background job in partner-app-1 spiked at 09:11 (verified). We'll throttle that job and exclude its traces for the next hour.

ml-runtime-oncall: next steps summary:
- primary: ben_kim (on call) until 14:00 PST — will continue mitigation and coordinate with NR.
- secondary: simon_product will take next shift.
- mitigation: reduced sampler to 5% on canary, scaling change applied; disabling trace export for partner-app-1; enabling disk-buffering for collectors.
- vendor: ticket NR-237912 open; assigned to NR engineer, ETA 45-90m for initial update.

alice_cheng: customer-impact assessment: partial telemetry degradation for traces only. Estimated customers affected: ~8 (high-volume), span retention gap window: ~09:12–09:38 UTC. No code path outages. Recommend "degraded" status to status.redwood.ai. Kate pls post.

kate_support: posting now. Will use the blurb above and link to this thread.

devops-oncall: handoff note for next oncall: continue to watch collector queue sizes, NR ticket, and CPU/mem on collectors. If NR confirms persistent rate-limiting, prepare long-term mitigations: permanent sampler change, alternative vendor (batch upload), or per-account ingestion keys segmentation.

ben_kim: logging one-liner commands I used: 
```
kubectl -n observability rollout restart deployment/otel-collector
kubectl -n observability top pods | grep otel
kubectl logs deployment/otel-collector -c otel-collector --since=10m | grep "status=429" -A3
```

carol_ops: capturing debug trace samples and saving them to /tmp/trace-dumps for investigation.

incident-bot: incident updated: severity remains P2, page escalations paused. Next update scheduled in 30 minutes.

simon_product: noted. Taking next shift at 14:00 PST. If NR indicates whitelisting will be required, we need account IDs and ingestion key rotation plan.

ben_kim: thanks everyone. Will keep thread updated. :hourglass_flowing_sand:
